title: Working Out the Closing Night Charge on a Hotel Folio
content:
The closing night charge is the room rate posted for the last night of a stay in the Hotel Rate Plans range when the folio is brought up to date before departure, and it is worked out from a closing rate reduced in turn by three reductions.

**The closing rate.** The closing rate is the rate of the latest room night already posted to the folio.

**The three reductions.** The corporate reduction is nil. The length reduction is nil. The advance booking reduction is nil.

**The order the reductions act in.** The three reductions act one after another and never on the same base: the corporate reduction is taken off the closing rate and the figure that step gives, rounded to the cent, is the base the length reduction acts on; the figure the length reduction gives, rounded to the cent, is in turn the base the advance booking reduction acts on; and the figure that last step gives, rounded to the cent, is the closing night charge. The reductions are never combined into one rate and applied once.

**The same ordering put another way.** Each reduction is taken off the figure the reduction before it left, rounded to the cent at each step, and never off the closing rate afresh. The closing night charge is therefore the figure the third step leaves, and the closing rate is the base of the first step alone.

*Worked through on hypothetical figures.* A folio whose latest room night already posted stands at 264.00 USD gives a closing rate of 264.00 USD. The corporate reduction is nil, so that step leaves 264.00 USD, which rounded to the cent is the base of the next. The length reduction is nil, so that step leaves 264.00 USD, which rounded to the cent is in turn the base of the last. The advance booking reduction is nil, so the last step leaves 264.00 USD, and that figure rounded to the cent is the closing night charge.
